project_goal: Make learned-zeroD full-PA tuning bypass legacy 3D steady seed generation and submit with a resource allocation consistent with its configured tuning parallelism.

decisions.statement: Redefine iteration1_seed.path as the required input 0D JSON for source=learned_zerod and remove implicit reduced steady generation from that branch.
Copy or stage the configured learned source into a canonical run-scoped provenance path before invocation, while preserving the patient source as read-only.
Use one pure tune-job CPU resolver for both script rendering and default Slurm submission, resolving to max(scheduler cpus, tuning n_procs).
Keep full-PA calibration as the existing explicit preop-select/postprocess/run-calibrate sequence in this change and document it clearly.

constraints.statement: Patient/Oak data is read-only and all generated artifacts remain under the configured runs_root.
Remote execution, transfer, and Slurm actions must continue through typed adapters.
The change must preserve source=generate reduced-seed behavior and source=path staging behavior.
Calibration automation is outside this corrective change because the repository documents it as a separate explicit workflow and integration gap.
No new dependency is warranted for source staging or CPU resolution.

invariants.statement: A learned_zerod run never invokes run_steady_sims or constructs legacy seed_generation preop/postop directories.
Missing or unreadable learned source input fails before learned-zeroD execution and never falls back to reduced steady generation.
The requested Slurm CPU count for the parent tune job equals the CPU count embedded in its rendered script and is at least impedance n_procs.
Generated inputs and provenance remain deterministic, inspectable, and run-scoped.

repository_evidence.finding: The learned helper currently calls _generate_iteration_seed, which creates preop/postop directories and runs steady simulations before invoking the upstream learned adapter.
repository_evidence.implications: TASK-001 must remove only the learned branch's dependency on _generate_iteration_seed while preserving explicit reduced generation.

repository_evidence.finding: The config model and patient asset resolver already provide an absolute iteration1 seed path, and existing typed transfer helpers stage remote seed inputs.
repository_evidence.implications: TASK-001 can reuse the current path and transfer boundaries without adding schema fields or dependencies.

repository_evidence.finding: Tune script rendering raises CPUs to tuning n_procs, but _build_default_adapters passes the raw scheduler default to sbatch, whose command-line option overrides the script directive.
repository_evidence.implications: TASK-002 must create one resolver and route the same value to renderer and default adapter.

repository_evidence.finding: Current documentation and code expose calibration as an explicit workflow that requires preop postprocess evidence; automatic chaining is not implemented.
repository_evidence.implications: Builders must not add automatic calibration or watch-loop authority as part of these tasks.

tasks.title: Make learned-zeroD consume the configured source directly
tasks.objective: Eliminate legacy steady/preop/postop seed generation from source=learned_zerod, stage or reference the configured input 0D JSON safely, fail fast when it is unavailable, and document the explicit learned/calibration contract.

in_scope: Carry the resolved iteration1_seed.path into learned runtime configuration.
Reuse existing typed transfer/staging behavior for local and remote source files where execution mode permits it.
Create a canonical run-scoped learned/source_0d_config.json copy before calling generate_full_pa_learned_seed.
Remove _generate_iteration_seed from the learned branch while preserving it for source=generate.
Add focused tests for local source staging, remote-only rendering/execution behavior, missing-source failure, compiled rendered blocks, and absence of learned steady scaffolding.
Update execution and patient-data documentation, including the explicit calibration continuation sequence.
out_of_scope: Changing svZeroDTrees scientific learned-seed generation or validation.
Automatically submitting preop postprocess or calibration jobs.
Selecting the scientifically authoritative TST-STAN-5 baseline on the user's behalf.
Deleting or mutating the active tst5-09212026 run.

affected_components: Iteration-1 learned seed staging and execution
implementation_notes: Treat iteration1_seed.path as the learned adapter's input 0D JSON when source=learned_zerod; do not introduce a second configuration key unless repository evidence makes reuse impossible, in which case escalate.
Preserve source=generate behavior exactly: _generate_iteration_seed remains available only for explicit reduced generation/fallback paths that already own it.
The remote driver must validate the learned source, create seed_generation/learned, copy the source to source_0d_config.json, and pass that copy to LearnedSeedGenerationConfig.
Do not create seed_generation/preop, seed_generation/postop, or seed_generation/steady in the learned branch.
Use existing RemoteExecAdapter/FileTransferAdapter boundaries for execute-time remote checks or transfers; no direct workflow subprocess/SSH/rsync calls.
Dry-run output must remain deterministic even when the configured source exists only on Oak.
Update existing assertions that currently expect sim.run_steady_sims in all rendered scripts so they distinguish learned and generated sources.
Document that calibration.enabled authorizes later explicit calibration but does not chain it automatically.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A rendered source=learned_zerod iteration uses the configured source 0D path or staged canonical source and contains no call from _generate_learned_iteration_seed to _generate_iteration_seed.
The learned path writes its provenance input only under the run-scoped seed_generation/learned directory and never creates learned seed_generation/preop, postop, or steady directories.
A missing learned source fails with a specific error before invoking learned-zeroD and never falls back to steady generation.
Existing source=generate and source=path tests continue to pass without changed semantics.
Execution and patient-data docs accurately describe required learned source input, run-scoped copying, no steady generation, and explicit calibration continuation.

verification.expected_result: All learned, generated, path, rendering, and patient-path tests pass.

verification.procedure: Inspect the source=learned_zerod helper and its rendered-script assertions for _generate_iteration_seed, run_steady_sims, seed_generation/preop, seed_generation/postop, and seed_generation/steady.
verification.expected_result: The learned helper contains none of the legacy generation calls or directory construction; explicit source=generate still contains the reduced generator.

escalation_conditions: The existing iteration1_seed.path cannot represent the learned source without breaking source=path or source=generate semantics.
Safe remote source handling would require bypassing typed adapters.
The upstream learned adapter actually requires newly generated steady-result artifacts beyond the input JSON and centerline.

tasks.title: Unify tune-job CPU rendering and submission
tasks.objective: Resolve the effective parent tune-job CPU count once and ensure the rendered #SBATCH directive and default Slurm submission options both use max(scheduler cpus, tuning n_procs).

in_scope: Introduce a focused pure resolver for effective tune CPUs.
Use the resolved value in script rendering and _build_default_adapters/SlurmSubmitOptions.
Preserve injected scheduler adapters and non-CPU scheduler defaults.
Add tests that capture the default submit command/options and compare them with the rendered header.
Document the tune workflow's single resource-resolution boundary.
out_of_scope: Changing cluster partition, memory, time, or account defaults.
Submitting or cancelling a real Sherlock job.

implementation_notes: Build on the integrated TASK-001 result because both tasks modify tune_trees.py and test_run_tune_dry_run.py.

The resolver must accept the validated scheduler CPU value and the effective tuning config; for impedance it returns max(default, n_procs), while behavior for configurations without n_procs must preserve the scheduler value.
Pass the resolved CPU count explicitly into both _render_tune_job_script and _build_default_adapters instead of recomputing it independently.
Do not modify src/svztagent/hpc/slurm.py unless a focused compatibility issue is proven; its generic override behavior is correct.
Tests must prove the actual default adapter submit options use 24 when scheduler cpus=4 and impedance n_procs=24, matching the script header.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: One shared resolver determines the effective tune-job CPU count used by both rendering and default Slurm adapter construction.
With scheduler cpus=4 and impedance n_procs=24, the rendered script and submitted Slurm options both request 24 CPUs.
Injected scheduler adapters remain supported and existing tune workflow tests pass.
Architecture documentation explains that the workflow, not the generic Slurm adapter, owns effective tune CPU resolution.

verification.expected_result: All tune rendering/submission and generic Slurm adapter tests pass.
Configuration and iteration execution regressions pass.

verification.procedure: Inspect the final tune workflow call graph and test evidence to confirm the same resolved CPU value reaches _render_tune_job_script and SlurmSubmitOptions.
verification.expected_result: There is no independent raw scheduler-cpus override on the default submission path.

escalation_conditions: The effective CPU policy cannot be represented without changing the public configuration schema.
A required fix would alter generic Slurm behavior for unrelated workflows.
Verification shows that impedance n_procs is not the correct allocation lower bound.

execution_groups.name: Learned source correction
execution_groups.concurrency_rationale: The learned source change establishes the staging and rendering baseline consumed by the later resource task.
conflict_controls: Run in an isolated worktree created from a snapshot of the current dirty main checkout.
Do not begin TASK-002 until TASK-001 is integrated because both own tune_trees.py and test_run_tune_dry_run.py.

execution_groups.name: Tune resource consistency
execution_groups.concurrency_rationale: Resource consistency is a separate behavior but shares central files, so it runs after the learned source correction is integrated.
conflict_controls: Create TASK-002's worktree from the integrated TASK-001 commit.
Limit edits to the task's declared resource resolver, tests, and architecture documentation.

integration_checkpoints.title: Learned seed contract integrated
integration_checkpoints.objective: Confirm learned input staging is fail-fast and contains no legacy steady/preop/postop path before building resource changes on top.

verification.expected_result: Learned, generated, and path seed tests all pass in the integrated branch.

integration_checkpoints.failure_action: Return TASK-001 to its Builder; do not start TASK-002 until the learned contract and tests pass.

integration_checkpoints.title: Combined local workflow verification
integration_checkpoints.objective: Verify learned source behavior and resource consistency together against the focused workflow suite.

verification.procedure: pytest -q tests/test_run_tune_dry_run.py tests/test_patient_path_resolution.py tests/test_slurm_adapter.py tests/test_config_loading.py tests/test_iteration_tracking.py
verification.expected_result: All focused workflow, path, scheduler, configuration, and iteration tests pass.
The combined Python source compiles successfully.

integration_checkpoints.failure_action: Identify which task introduced the failure and return only that task for revision; do not run a production Sherlock smoke test.

risks.description: The operator may select a technically valid but scientifically incorrect TST-STAN-5 baseline.
risks.mitigation: Require an explicit configured path and preserve/digest the run-scoped source; leave baseline selection to the user/operator.

risks.description: Remote-only source behavior may differ between dry-run and execute staging.
risks.mitigation: Test both deterministic dry-run rendering and fake-adapter execute preflight/staging.

risks.description: Changing CPU resolution may unintentionally affect non-impedance or injected-adapter paths.
risks.mitigation: Use a pure resolver, preserve injection, and run generic Slurm plus iteration regression tests.

risks.description: The user's main checkout contains overlapping uncommitted work.
risks.mitigation: Build from an orchestrator-created snapshot commit in serial isolated worktrees and leave the main worktree untouched until reviewed integration.

open_questions.question: Should the replacement TST-STAN-5 run use baseline_0d.json or a newly curated zerod-models/baseline_0d_learned.json?
open_questions.impact: The answer determines the workspace path used for the production smoke run but does not change the implementation contract.
